question.text: 'Narmada Credit Opportunities Fund' is a Category II AIF with a target corpus of INR 400 crore. Under Regulation 10(d) of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the minimum continuing interest the Manager or Sponsor is required to maintain in the scheme?

answer.text: INR 5 crore (fixed), regardless of corpus size
2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is lower — i.e. INR 5 crore in this case
5% of corpus or INR 10 crore, whichever is lower — i.e. INR 10 crore in this case
10% of corpus uniformly applicable to all categories

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 10(d) prescribes continuing interest for Category I and II AIFs at 2.5% of corpus OR INR 5 crore, whichever is lower. For a INR 400 crore corpus: 2.5% = INR 10 crore; lower of (INR 10 cr, INR 5 cr) = INR 5 crore. The cap 'whichever is lower' deliberately prevents large funds from locking in excessive GP capital. The Trap: Option A drops the 2.5% calculation — wrong for a small fund where 2.5% is below INR 5 cr. Option C applies the Category III rule (5%/INR 10 cr) — the most common confusion. Option D is fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A focuses on 'Cat I/II has skin-in-the-game' as a selling point. XIX-C requires exact computation and knowledge that the rule differs from Cat III. XXI-B (PM) has no equivalent sponsor-commitment rule. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Sponsor commitment cannot be through waiver of management fees — it must be actual capital invested in the scheme. This is commonly disclosed as 'GP Commitment' in the PPM and is locked-in at First Close; it cannot be withdrawn or transferred post-First-Close.
